findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices and inverted equality check
findings.body: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the encoded prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`0..2` session type, `2..4` token type, `4..6` grant type), as decoded in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` with `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. However, line 483 checks `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. This has two bugs: (1) `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type and the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"` from `"onrtac"`) instead of `substring(4, 6)`, and (2) the condition is missing a negation (`!`), so it returns `false` when the shortcut matches and `true` when it does not. Because `substring(3, 5)` never equals any of the expected grant shortcuts, the `if` branch is never taken and the matcher silently passes for any grant type.

findings.title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: In `AccessTokenContext(SessionType, TokenType, String, String)`, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. Passing a `null` `rawTokenId` will not be rejected by the constructor.

findings.title: Javadoc states grant shortcut is 3 letters while encoder requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the entire prefix (`sessionType` + `tokenType` + `grantType`) to be 6 characters and slices the grant shortcut at `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`. Any `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation that follows the Javadoc and returns a 3-letter shortcut will produce 7-character prefixes that fail decoding with `IllegalArgumentException: Incorrect token id ... Expected length of 6`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory instead of testing unknown grant rejection
findings.body: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()`, `factory.postInit(...)` is not called, leaving `factory.sessionFactory` as `null`. When `testIncorrectGrantType()` looks up the unregistered `"ac"` shortcut, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut` attempts to call `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a `NullPointerException` before `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` can throw `IllegalArgumentException`. Catching `RuntimeException` hides the `NullPointerException` and leaves the `IllegalArgumentException` path untested.
